vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: here-now
Version: 1.6.3

The skill is classified as suspicious due to two primary reasons: 1) The `SKILL.md` and `scripts/publish.sh` recommend installing `jq` via `curl -fsSL https://here.now/install.sh | bash` if it's not found or bundled. While this is a common installation pattern, it represents a significant supply chain vulnerability (remote code execution risk) if the `here.now` domain or the `install.sh` script were compromised. 2) The `scripts/publish.sh` includes an `--allow-nonherenow-base-url` flag which, when explicitly passed, allows the skill to send the API key to an arbitrary base URL. Although there's a security check to prevent accidental exfiltration, this capability, if misused by an attacker controlling the arguments, could lead to credential exfiltration. These are risky capabilities without clear malicious intent from the skill itself.

llm.summary: The skill's requirements, instructions, and included script are consistent with a static-hosting

dimensions.detail: Name/description (publish static files) matches what the script and docs do: build a manifest, request presigned upload URLs, upload files, finalize, and store local state and optional API key. Required binaries (curl, file, jq) and optional HERENOW_API_KEY / ~/.herenow/credentials are appropriate for this purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions stick to publishing flows (create/update publish, upload, finalize, store state). Two items worth noting: (1) the script accepts --base-url and a --allow-nonherenow-base-url override which—if used—will allow an API key to be sent to a non-default endpoint (the script defaults to refusing such sends). (2) The SKILL.md instructs agents to ask users for email to send a magic link and then to have users copy the API key from the dashboard; it also instructs storing the API key in ~/.herenow/credentials. These are expected for this feature but are the primary points where user secrets are introduced.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: This is instruction-only with an included publish.sh script (no automated installer). The script will error if jq is missing and suggests running a curl | bash install helper at https://here.now/install.sh — that is a manual instruction presented in an error message and not executed by the skill itself. Users should treat running remote install scripts as sensitive.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Only an optional HERENOW_API_KEY and a local credentials file are requested. No unrelated secrets or system configuration paths are required. The script reads ~/.herenow/credentials and may write .herenow/state.json in the working directory; both are proportional to the publish workflow.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Skill is not always-enabled and does not request elevated platform privileges. It only writes its own local state (~/.herenow and ./ .herenow) and does not modify other skills or global agent config.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to do what it says: publish static files to the here.now service. Before installing or running it: 1) Verify you trust the here.now service and the package source (the skill references https://here.now). 2) Do not paste API keys on the command line; follow the credential-file guidance and protect ~/.herenow/credentials (the skill also warns about this). 3) Avoid running remote install scripts (curl | bash) unless you trust the URL; the script only suggests such a command when jq is missing. 4) Be careful with the --base-url and --allow-nonherenow-base-url flags — they allow sending your API key to a custom endpoint and should be used only with trusted endpoints. 5) If you plan to let an autonomous agent operate this skill, understand it can upload any files you give it and save claim tokens in the local state file; do not give it secrets or files you do not want published.
